Urban Mycelium

Imagining Living Urban Ecologies Through Augmented Reality

In this project

Project briefKeywordsDrawings & outcomesMy roleToolsCollaborators

Project brief

Urban Mycelium is a speculative design project developed during a one-week augmented reality (AR) workshop, exploring how urban infrastructure might evolve into a living, interconnected ecological network. Inspired by fungal systems and bioluminescent organisms, the project imagines hybrid structures that blur the boundaries between nature, technology, and architecture. Two speculative designs—Aerolume, a floating air-purifying organism, and Glowstool, a luminous urban seating structure—were digitally modelled using Blender and ZBrush, then brought into augmented reality through 8th Wall. By placing these imagined organisms within real-world environments, the project explores how AR can bridge speculative design and everyday urban experience. Through digital modelling and immersive visualisation, Urban Mycelium reimagines the city as an evolving ecological system, using augmented reality to explore alternative relationships between urban infrastructure, natural organisms, and public life.
